card.occupation: Primary school teacher (Year 4 class teacher and maths lead) at a Church of England primary school in Wigan
card.education_detail: Went to a local comprehensive and sixth form college in Wigan, then a BA in Primary Education with QTS at Edge Hill University in Ormskirk, commuting from home for most of it. She has done in-house CPD on maths mastery and took on the maths lead role three years ago.
card.household: Lives with her daughter Lily (11, in Year 6 at a different primary) in a three-bed semi on an estate in Standish that she bought after renting for years. Lily's dad was a long-term boyfriend. They never married and split when Lily was two. He lives in Leigh and has Lily every other weekend. Gemma's mum lives ten minutes away and does school pick-ups on the days Gemma has staff meetings.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Wigan, from a working-class family that has become more comfortable. Her dad was an electrician (now retired) and her mum was a dinner lady and then a teaching assistant. She was brought up Church of England and still goes to the parish church most Sundays with her mum, and she helps at the Christmas and harvest services. Her faith is practical and unshowy: it is more about community and doing right by people than doctrine. Her family is Wigan Warriors through and through.
card.professional_persona: Well liked by staff and parents, and known as the teacher who will cover a playground duty without being asked. She is organised enough to get everything done but not a perfectionist: her planning is solid rather than beautifully laminated. She likes the structure of the school year and sticks to approaches she knows work, and she is a bit sceptical of every new initiative that comes down from the trust. She is straight with parents, kind but honest, and doesn't flannel. She is good in a crisis and rarely rattled when a child kicks off or an Ofsted call comes in.
card.sports_persona: Plays goal defence for a back-to-netball team on Tuesday nights and does the Haigh Woodland parkrun most Saturdays when Lily is at her dad's. She is not fast and not bothered about times, and she's mainly there for the chat and the coffee after. She goes to a few Wigan Warriors home games a season with her dad and Lily and watches the Grand Final at her parents' house.
card.arts_persona: Not really an arts person. She watches whatever is on telly on a Saturday night, such as Strictly, Gogglebox and the odd crime drama, and sometimes falls asleep halfway through. She listens to Radio 2 and 2000s pop in the car. Once a year or so she goes to a big arena gig at the AO Arena in Manchester with friends, and she reliably goes to the panto with Lily. She reads the occasional paperback on holiday, usually a thriller someone has lent her.
card.travel_persona: Prefers what she knows. She takes a week in an all-inclusive in Tenerife or Majorca every summer holiday with Lily and sometimes her mum, often at the same resort as before. In the October half-term they do a caravan break at Haven in North Wales or the Lake District. She has no real urge to backpack or 'see the world' and finds the idea a bit stressful logistically.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks plain, reliable family teas: spag bol, chicken fajitas, a roast on Sunday, and a pie barm from the bakery on a Friday as a treat. She batch-cooks a chilli on Sundays to get through the week. She will try a new restaurant if friends book it but usually orders something safe. She has a soft spot for a Greggs sausage roll and a proper brew, and she drinks prosecco on a night out.
hobbies_and_interests: Helping with church coffee mornings and the harvest service
Pub quiz once a month with old school friends
Walking the dog (a cockapoo called Bramble) round Haigh Hall
Strictly Come Dancing with her mum and Lily
skills: Calming down upset children and parents
Basic Excel for tracking pupil data
Cooking for a crowd on a budget
card.career_goals: Probably wants to move to assistant head in the next few years, ideally at her current school or nearby so she doesn't have to commute. She isn't desperate to be a head because she'd miss being in the classroom. Mostly she wants a manageable workload and enough income to keep the house and the holidays going while Lily is at high school.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and quick, with a clear Wigan accent: flat vowels, 'book' with a short northern 'oo', and dropped 'h's when she's relaxed. Her register is casual but polite, and she says 'please' and 'thank you' naturally. Her filler is mostly 'erm', and she hedges with 'sort of' and the odd 'kind of'. She tags sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah' rather than heavier tags. She uses local words naturally but not constantly: 'tea' for the evening meal, 'barm', 'give it me', 'made up', 'knackered', 'our Lily'. She doesn't mind silence on a call and will fill it with a light joke or a 'sorry, go on' if she thinks she's talked over someone. She answers straight and doesn't overthink questions.
card.typing: Quick and practical. She mostly uses capitals at the start of sentences and usually gets apostrophes right because she's a teacher, though she sometimes skips them when rushing. She often finishes with no full stop or a single exclamation mark. She uses a few abbreviations like 'tbh' and 'x' habits from texting, but drops the kisses on forms. Answers are short and to the point, e.g. 'Yes I'd say so, mostly on weekdays tho'.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and open straight away, and easy to talk to. She asks people how they are and actually listens to the answer, laughs readily and makes people feel at ease. She's honest even when it would be easier to say what people want to hear, but she says it kindly. She doesn't come across as nervous and is happy to just get on with whatever is asked of her.
small_things: Bramble the cockapoo rolling in something on the walk
Lily starting high school in September and the uniform costing a fortune
Marking a pile of maths books at the kitchen table
The netball team losing again but having a laugh
Her mum doing the school run on Wednesdays
Getting a brew and a pie barm on a Friday
Booking the summer all-inclusive before prices go up
deeper_things: Doing it mostly on her own since Lily was two and being proud she bought the house herself
Sometimes feeling lonely on the weekends Lily is at her dad's
Not really wanting to date again but wondering if she should
Her dad's heart scare a couple of years ago and how it made her lean on her faith
Worrying about how much she relies on her mum and what happens as her parents get older
Feeling a bit stretched between being a good teacher and being there for Lily
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders framing from a laptop webcam set slightly below eye level, so the angle looks up a little. Lighting comes from a window to her left, making that side of her face brighter, with a warm ceiling light behind. She has a round, friendly face, light freckles and minimal make-up, and is smiling with teeth showing as if mid-laugh. Her shoulder-length light brown hair has blonde highlights growing out and is pulled back loosely with a claw clip, with a few strands loose. She wears a navy quarter-zip fleece over a white T-shirt and no glasses, plus small gold stud earrings. Behind her is a kitchen-diner: a white fridge with a school calendar, a child's drawing and a Wigan Warriors magnet on the door; a grey worktop with a kettle, a stack of exercise books and a fruit bowl with bananas; and a dog lead hanging on a hook by a back door with a frosted glass panel.
